short: Storybook's stories, docs pages and frame
is: The component gallery's content in Storybook: Svelte CSF stories files (`<group>/<Name>.stories.svelte`), MDX docs pages (`<group>/<Name>.mdx`), made-up fixtures (`fixtures/*.ts`), and `frame/`, the decorator every story renders in, which carries the toolbar's Skin and Motion choices onto the page.
conventions: A stories file imports only `@storybook/addon-svelte-csf`, `storybook/test` and `@zurfur/ui` by its public entry, plus relative files under `src/stories/` and `src/gallery/`; a path into `src/lib/`, `bits-ui` or any other package is refused (`src/checks/story-imports.spec.ts`). Stories carry no `<style>`, `style=` or `style:` and no `a11y` or `backgrounds` setting: looks come from the components and the frame. A docs story height or iframe height is only a constant from `controls/room.ts`, each of which is a whole number of rem.

Every string and text in a stories file is held to the docs-text rule, since Storybook renders a story's docs description as Markdown with raw HTML: no URL or `//` anywhere, no HTML tag outside inline code spans, and no Markdown link or image destination a browser reads as remote (`src/checks/story-imports.spec.ts`). A keyboard map is a plain list, `- Key: what it does`.

A story renders its control alone, or composed with other `@zurfur/ui` components, never hand-built markup standing in for one. A control that follows only its parent (`value`, `checked` or `open`) is shown through `controls/<Name>Holder.svelte`, which keeps what the control asks for, hands each callback to the story's spy first, and renders only that control with no style and no spread; the meta's `component` stays the control, so autodocs shows its props. A story that turns a surface on after it mounts uses a helper in `surfaces/` instead, and unlike the one-control holders it renders three: `LoadingHolder.svelte` draws a Button, a Spinner status mounted empty from the start and Skeleton lines once loading starts, keeps only whether loading has started, and hands the press to the story's spy first. Every control is a simple component but Scrolling Tabs, a composite; a stories file's tags name its kind (`simple` or `composite`), and its description opens with it.

Stories compose: a stories file or a story helper renders no owned element (`button`, `a`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `img`, `video`, `audio`, `iframe`, SVG `image`, and SVG `set`, `animate`, `animateMotion`, `animateTransform` and `feImage`, which no file renders), writes no `zf-` class and renders no `link`, `base`, `<svelte:head>` or nested `<style>`; the Paper token page's bare buttons are listed by exact path in `src/checks/composition-table.ts`. Each stories file's `defineMeta.tags` carries its component's kind, `simple` or `composite`, beside `autodocs`, and a stories file with no library component, like a token page, carries neither (`src/checks/composition.spec.ts`).

The folder is ESLint's `stories` file set, in the gallery host tier: the host's bans hold (no `fetch`, no storage, no remote or `javascript:` string, no raw HTML, no script markup, no inline handler, no dynamic import).

A docs page (`.mdx`, allowed only under `src/stories/`) holds only `import { Meta, Story } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';`, `import * as X from './<Name>.stories.svelte';` from its own folder, one `<Meta of={X} />`, Markdown headings, plain prose, blank lines and `<Story of={X.<Story>} />` lines; any other import or JSX, `{` outside `of={…}`, `export`, an image, a link, raw HTML or a URL is refused (`src/checks/docs-pages.spec.ts`).

Every component `src/lib/index.ts` exports has a stories file whose `defineMeta.component` is that component imported from `@zurfur/ui`, and a contract spec; a pending list names the controls still waiting for stories and may only shrink (`src/checks/story-coverage.spec.ts`). Fixtures and stories files carry only the reserved sample DID and handles ending in `.test` or `.example`, a bare domain in a handle-named field, variable or attribute is refused too, and a stories file that does not parse is refused (`src/checks/story-fixtures.spec.ts`, which reads every file under `src/stories/` and `src/gallery/`, docs pages and node files included).

Titles and story names are in Title Case ("Tokens and Paper/Colour", "Controls/Button"): each word of every `defineMeta` title segment, every `<Story name>` and every fixture `title` string starts with a capital, but for a, an, and, of, the, to, in, on, for, with and by after the first word, and a word that starts with a digit or a symbol; a title or name that isn't one string, and a stories file with no title, are refused (`src/checks/story-coverage.spec.ts`, whose pending list of fixture titles only shrinks). No middle dot and no age-check words anywhere here (`src/checks/words.spec.ts`). The sidebar order is `.storybook/preview.ts`'s.
Storybook and the Vitest story projects run only through the package's scripts, under `env -i` and the network guard (see `frontend/ui`).
entry_points: frame/StoryFrame.svelte (the decorator every story renders in)

fs.name: controls/
fs.role: the controls' stories: <Name>.stories.svelte for each of the twelve exported components (autodocs, a Playground, and play functions for the pointer, the keyboard, disabled and busy, plus a Focused story), <Name>Holder.svelte for each control that follows only its parent, args.ts (each template's args: the control's own props) and room.ts (the room a docs page gives a story whose floating part opens below it)

fs.name: fixtures/
fs.role: made-up words, options and days the stories share, readonly and typed: actions.ts (Button, Icon Button, Checkbox, Toggle, Pill Switch) and fields.ts (Text Input, Select, Tabs, Scrolling Tabs, Menu, Date Field) and surfaces.ts (the surfaces and feedback pieces, with the fixture picture and the pins' points minted by their guards), and PlaceholderArt.svelte (an obvious placeholder picture of plain shapes in token colours, read out by the label it is given, with no load of its own; what it is given sits on it, placed against its box, as Pin's stories place their pins)

fs.name: frame/
fs.role: StoryFrame.svelte (sets data-skin and data-motion on <html> and on a wrapping div, the portal target, from the toolbar's globals, and paints a docs page's background and text from the skin's tokens; a story tagged `layer` gets `layer`, which contains the wrapper's layout and paint at a dialog's height, so a fixed layer stays inside its story), FrameSkin.svelte (resolves Follow the OS to the skin showing), globals.ts (parseSkinChoice and parseMotion: address text to closed unions, unknown text meaning Follow the OS and Lively) and their specs

fs.name: surfaces/
fs.role: the surfaces and feedback pieces' stories, under "Surfaces and Feedback": <Name>.stories.svelte for each exported surface (Card, Badge, Spinner, Skeleton, Avatar, VisibilityMarker, StatusPill, Pin, ToastStack), each tagged with its kind, with a Moves and Sounds story for the moving ones; ToastStack's also carries `layer` and `phone-320`; and LoadingHolder.svelte, the helper for Skeleton's With a Status story (a Button that turns on a Spinner status mounted empty from the start, and Skeleton lines while it loads)

fs.name: tokens/
fs.role: the six token pages as docs pages: <Name>Page.svelte (the page body, also rendered by the old gallery's route wrapper), <Name>.stories.svelte (one Page story, showing only the skin the toolbar picks) and <Name>.mdx (its docs page), for Colour, Type, Space and Shape, Shadows, Motion and Sound, Paper
